digest.component_or_area: rebar reconciler git mutation policy gate (check_raw_git_writes.py)
propositions: The existing raw-git-write checker (R1/R2, policy d37e) passes clean but misses out-of-seam composition: reconciler calls like git_adapter.add + git_adapter.commit in reconcile_helpers.py:226/246 are approved call-by-call as sanctioned exports but violate the protocol that tracker mutations must be atomic.

R3 rule must fire on a mutation-primitive call (add, commit, commit_tree, read_tree, rm_cached, update_ref, write_tree) made from outside the reconciler write-seam modules (git_adapter.py, _ref_lock.py, _ref_lock_push.py) where the receiver is a resolved git-adapter module reference (import binding or dynamic-loader binding).
R3 must not fire on non-git-adapter .add/.commit calls, read-only exports (e.g., git_adapter.commit_email which is git log, not a mutation), or inside the three sanctioned seam-internal files.

Out-of-seam composition sites take durable reasoned inline markers: reconcile_helpers.py:226/246 (_commit_binding_store_snapshot) cites blocking behavior from rerouting through push.commit_and_push_tickets_branch; __main__.py:338-351 (_purge_committed_reconciler_locks) cites detached-index CAS concurrency-safety which is not statically decidable from the callable.

The gate implementation adds R3 to the existing checker in scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py, reuses the # raw-git-ok: marker vocabulary for sanction, adds unit tests to enforce the rule without false positives on ordinary .add/.commit calls, and ensures zero unsanctioned violations on the real tree before landing.
